appraisal_events.evidence: "Peut-être aussi Charlus, de qui l'insolence était un don de nature qu'il avait joie à exercer, profitait-il de la minute pendant laquelle il était censé ignorer qui était le nom de ces deux jeunes gens pour se divertir aux dépens de Mme de Surgis... comme Scapin met à profit le déguisement de son maître pour lui administrer des volées de coups de bâton."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator speculatively suggests Charlus's feigned ignorance of the young men lets him mock Mme de Surgis for sport, likening him to Scapin, a low comic trickster who beats his disguised master — a discrediting comparison, though explicitly hedged as conjecture ("peut-être").

status_effects.explanation: Charlus is portrayed as insincere and enjoying cruelty toward Mme de Surgis under a pretense of ignorance, mildly diminishing him, though the narrator frames this as speculative rather than certain.

ambiguities: The passage's essayistic reflection on nephews resembling their 'uncles' and on 'Messieurs de Charlus' as a type gestures toward Charlus's hidden nature, but this is generalizing commentary about a type rather than a discrete local event targeting the character, so it was not scored as a separate event.
